title: Boluda Towage acquires Dutch offshore towage specialist Muller Dordrecht
summary: Boluda Towage took full ownership of Muller Dordrecht, a Dutch marine services firm founded in 1918 that operates 16 tugs (including 7 offshore tugs) and 8 barges for offshore and coastal towage, heavy transport and marine project work. The business will trade as Boluda Muller Towage alongside Boluda Towage Europe; financial terms were not disclosed. The deal adds offshore/project towage capability to the world's largest harbour towage operator, extending Boluda's reach beyond port towage into the offshore segment where P&O Maritime and Smit Lamnalco also compete.

title: Smit Lamnalco (Boskalis) starts construction of four DP2 offshore terminal support vessels for ExxonMobil Guyana
summary: Keel-laying at Uzmar Shipyard in Turkey marked the start of construction of four 60 m diesel-electric DP2 offshore terminal support vessels (Robert Allan RAmpage 6000DE design, 135 t bollard pull, FiFi1, oil-recovery capability, 60+ days endurance) for Boskalis subsidiary Smit Lamnalco. The vessels will support tankers loading crude from ExxonMobil's FPSOs offshore Guyana, with the first delivery due November 2027 and the rest in 2028. Contract value and charter duration were not disclosed. The programme consolidates Smit Lamnalco's position in the fast-growing Guyana offshore terminal support market, a niche where P&O Maritime also competes.
location: Offshore Guyana (vessels built at Uzmar, Kocaeli, Turkey)
capacity: 4 x 60 m DP2 terminal support vessels, 135 t bollard pull

title: Gulftainer's GT Lines formalises UAE-China partnerships: five-vessel KCX1 consortium and new KCX5 (CGX) service with CULines
summary: GT Lines, Gulftainer's shipping arm, announced vessel-sharing partnerships with Chinese carriers to anchor China-Khorfakkan trade. Beyond the already-upgraded KCX1 (two GT Lines vessels in a five-ship VSA with Zhong Gu, Sea Legend and Ningbo Ocean on Qingdao-Shanghai-Ningbo-Nansha-Khorfakkan, 18-22 day transits), GT Lines will also work with CULines on the KCX5 / CGX service rotating Qingdao-Ningbo-Shekou-Nansha-Port Klang-Khorfakkan. All arrangements start in early November 2026, adding a second China loop into Khorfakkan and strengthening the terminal as an Asia-Gulf gateway outside the Strait of Hormuz, in direct competition with DP World's Jebel Ali feeder and mainline flows.
capacity: KCX1: five-vessel consortium, 10-day frequency; KCX5/CGX: additional China-Port Klang-Khorfakkan loop

title: Gulftainer rebrands Sajaa dry port as Sharjah Dry Ports after record 150,000 TEU month
summary: Gulftainer renamed its flagship 70-hectare bonded inland facility at Sajaa (launched December 2025, about 90 km from Khorfakkan Port) as Sharjah Dry Ports, after it handled a record 150,000 TEUs in a single month. The site offers a 50,000 sqm interlocked yard, 5,000 sqm of warehousing and 30,000 sqm of bulk and container storage, with bonded storage, cold-chain and planned rail connectivity. The rebrand positions the facility as the inland gateway for the Northern Emirates and complements Gulftainer's Al Dhaid multimodal corridor, giving it an inland-port network that competes with DP World's Jebel Ali/Jafza hinterland offering.
capacity: 70 ha site; record 150,000 TEU handled in one month

title: Cochin Shipyard shareholders approve transfer of Kochi ISRF into 50:50 JV with Drydocks World
summary: Cochin Shipyard Ltd's postal ballot closed on 7 November 2026 with 99.99% approval for the special resolution to transfer its International Ship Repair Facility (ISRF) at Willingdon Island, Kochi, as a slump sale (minimum INR 1,800 crore, about USD 188m, paid half in cash and half in JV shares) into a new 50:50 joint venture with Drydocks World – Dubai FZCO (DP World); the related-party transaction resolution also passed with 99.98%. The ISRF has a 6,000 t shiplift, ~1,400 m of berthing and capacity for six vessels simultaneously, with plans to expand from 6 to 16 workstations; Drydocks World will nominate three of five directors and the CEO/CFO. Government, DIPAM and Cochin Port approvals remain, with closing targeted before FY-end March 2027. Shareholder clearance removes a key hurdle to DP World's entry into Indian ship repair via Cochin Shipyard.
capacity: 6,000 t shiplift, ~1,400 m berthing, 6 vessels at a time (expanding to 16 workstations)

title: Gulftainer opens Fujairah-Sharjah bonded corridor with inland customs clearance at Sharjah Dry Ports
summary: Gulftainer launched a bonded logistics corridor linking its Fujairah Terminal on the UAE east coast with Sharjah Dry Ports in Sajaa, allowing cargo to move under customs control and clear inland in Sharjah instead of at the port of arrival, with 12 days of free storage included. The product gives importers an east-coast-to-inland route that avoids the Strait of Hormuz and extends Gulftainer's multi-gateway model (Khorfakkan, Fujairah, Sharjah Dry Ports, Al Dhaid), competing with DP World's Jebel Ali-centred clearance and World Logistics Passport offering. Volumes, frequency and transit times were not disclosed.

title: APSEZ among three qualified bidders for Rs 11,733 crore VOC Port outer harbour marine works (Thoothukudi)
summary: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (APSEZ), Megha Engineering & Infrastructures and Vishwa Samudra Engineering are the three bidders competing for the Rs 11,733.28 crore Hybrid Annuity Model package covering breakwaters, capital dredging, reclamation and two 1,000 m berths for the outer harbour at V.O. Chidambaranar Port, Tamil Nadu. APSEZ qualifies on the strength of its 2.96 km Vizhinjam breakwater after the port authority replaced its dredging criterion with a breakwater-experience requirement. The marine works underpin a separate 30-year DBFOT concession for two container terminals totalling 5.2 million TEU with 18 m draft, positioning VOC as India's first east-coast transshipment hub to compete with Colombo. No award has been made; the overall project is appraised at about Rs 17,167 crore.
location: V.O. Chidambaranar Port, Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu
capacity: Marine works for two container terminals totalling 5.2 million TEU; 18 m draft; two 1,000 m berths

title: Boluda Shipping agrees to acquire Matrans Terminal Rotterdam in Eemhaven
summary: Boluda Shipping announced on 10 November (agreement signed 3 November) that it will acquire the Matrans multipurpose terminal in Rotterdam's Eemhaven, a key European short-sea hub: 360,000 m2 of land including 70,000 m2 of covered warehousing, 1,100 m of quay at 12.65 m depth, a ro-ro berth and 600 m of rail track, handling containers, forest products, metals, project cargo and ro-ro. Terms were not disclosed and the deal is subject to regulatory approval. Together with the October agreement to buy Samskip, it would give Boluda 21 maritime and 5 rail terminals and strengthens its sea-rail-road intermodal network in Northern Europe, competing with DP World's Rotterdam World Gateway and European intermodal footprint.
capacity: 360,000 m2 terminal; 1,100 m quay at 12.65 m; 70,000 m2 warehousing; 600 m rail

title: DHL Global Forwarding names Sascha Geiken CEO for Sub-Saharan Africa
summary: DHL Global Forwarding appointed Sascha Geiken, previously VP Ocean Freight Middle East & Africa and a former managing director across several Gulf markets, as CEO Sub-Saharan Africa (excluding South Africa), succeeding Egidio Monteiro and reporting to MEA CEO Tobias Maier. The appointment lands as DHL Group deploys the EUR 300m+ Sub-Saharan Africa investment programme announced in October 2025 across Express, Global Forwarding and Supply Chain (gateways, cold chain, warehousing in Nigeria, Ethiopia, South Africa). It signals a push on ocean freight, customs and inland reliability in African corridors where DP World competes through its ports and logistics arms.

title: ASRY partners with stc Bahrain to deploy Bahrain's first commercial private 5G network for yard automation
summary: ASRY and stc Bahrain agreed to deploy Bahrain's first commercial private 5G network across the ASRY shipyard to underpin AI-driven industrial IoT: AI surveillance, digital twins for asset performance, autonomous inspection robots and automated hull cleaning, welding and surface preparation. No financial terms were disclosed. The move is a yard-modernisation step aimed at faster, data-driven repair operations as ASRY competes with Drydocks World and IMI for Gulf ship-repair and offshore work.

title: Boluda Towage wins 10-year Port of Bunbury towage contract, displacing Svitzer
summary: Southern Ports and the Western Australian government awarded Boluda Towage a 10-year harbour towage contract at the Port of Bunbury following a competitive tender; Boluda replaces incumbent Svitzer Australia when its contract expires in December 2026. Boluda will deploy two new IMO Tier III tugs (first due December 2026, second February 2027) with interim cover from its Esperance fleet. Bunbury, the world's largest lithium export port (16.9 Mt, 418 calls last year), becomes Boluda's ninth Australian port after its 2025 acquisition of Mackenzie Marine and Towage in Esperance. Contract value was not disclosed. The win marks a direct market-share loss for Svitzer in Australia and continued Boluda consolidation in a market where DP World's P&O Maritime also operates.

title: DHL Express breaks ground on EUR 55m+ Stockholm Arlanda gateway for Sweden
summary: DHL Express and Nordic developer Slattö (via its Evolv logistics platform) started construction of a 14,000 sqm purpose-built gateway at Arlanda Stad next to Stockholm Arlanda Airport, an investment of more than EUR 55 million by DHL Express under a 15-year lease. The automated hub will sort up to 6,000 shipments per hour with 60 direct-loading positions and support for electric delivery vans, and is due to open in 2028 as DHL Express's new national gateway for Sweden. It follows DHL's EUR 100m Helsinki-Vantaa gateway (2025) and SEK 2bn Swedish e-commerce investment plan, deepening the Nordic express network in a market where DP World has just launched freight forwarding.
capacity: 14,000 sqm; 6,000 shipments/hour sorting; 60 direct-loading positions; operational 2028

title: Maersk opens USD 20m+ integrated logistics facility near Port of Montevideo, Uruguay
summary: Maersk inaugurated a 71,000 sqm integrated logistics facility on the Route 1 corridor near the Port of Montevideo, a fully private investment of more than USD 20 million, with Uruguay's President Yamandu Orsi and the transport minister attending. The site combines an empty-container depot (7,000 TEU storage, M&R, inspection, 140 reefer plugs) with 3,200 sqm of covered cargo handling, 1,000+ pallet positions, stuffing/de-stuffing and value-added services, and targets LEED Gold. It extends Maersk's Latin America landside build-out (Manzanillo, Suape, Brazil depots, Panama Pacifico) and strengthens its position at Montevideo, a free-port transhipment hub on the River Plate where DP World does not operate a terminal.
location: Montevideo (Camino Cibils / Camino Burghi, Route 1 corridor)
capacity: 71,000 sqm site; 3,200 sqm covered handling/storage; 7,000 TEU container storage; 1,000+ pallet positions; 140 reefer plugs; 6 inbound + 6 outbound gates

title: Yilport tables proposal to revise its Taranto container terminal concession; port authority to respond within 10-15 days
summary: Yilport Holding has submitted a proposal to the Port Network Authority of the Ionian Sea to revise the terms of its San Cataldo Container Terminal concession at Taranto, and the authority said it will answer within 10 to 15 days. The move follows a year of friction: the authority moved in September 2026 to call in Yilport's EUR 3 million guarantee over unmet commitments, while Yilport insists the long-promised dredging of the Molo Polisettoriale is essential before further investment. The outcome will decide whether Yilport keeps its only Italian deep-sea terminal, a Mediterranean asset relevant to DP World's own southern Europe footprint.
partners: Port Network Authority of the Ionian Sea (AdSP Mar Ionio)

title: Boluda Towage enters Ecuador with acquisition of Guayaquil tug operator Cititug
summary: Boluda Towage acquired Cititug, a Guayaquil-based towage and marine assistance company with over 20 years of operations and a five-tug fleet (Esperanza I, ASD Santa Fe, ASD Mater, ASD Alyssa, Valentina) covering harbour and sea towage, escort, offshore, salvage and oil-terminal/SPM assistance. Financial terms were not disclosed. The deal marks Boluda's entry into Ecuador and extends its Latin American network along South America's Pacific coast, where DP World operates the Posorja deep-water port near Guayaquil.

title: Port of Antwerp-Bruges International, Prumo and H2Uppp sign EUR 400k study agreement for low-carbon pipeline network at Port of Acu
summary: Prumo Logistica (operator of Brazil's Port of Acu), Port of Antwerp-Bruges International and the German-backed H2Uppp programme signed a EUR 400,000 agreement to fund a pre-feasibility study on shared pipeline infrastructure linking hydrogen and low-carbon fuel hubs to the Acu Liquids Terminal and the wider Acu complex. The deal deepens Port of Antwerp-Bruges International's long-standing involvement at Acu (where it holds a minority stake alongside Prumo) and advances the Antwerp-Acu green-corridor concept for ammonia and e-fuels, a decarbonised energy-trade niche that DP World has not yet entered in Brazil.
location: Port of Acu, Sao Joao da Barra, Rio de Janeiro
